normalization_and_gloss_notes: All reserved form spellings and source normalizations follow the reconciled contract/source proposal. The new words are not silently converted to Fulk overpoint spelling.
Fulk pronunciation overpoints are removed from the selected c/g examples, while source forms remain in the proposal and the amendments above. Cook gīet/regn spellings are retained.
Existing hǣlðu and forðām use the already declared thorn-to-eth course normalization; this revision does not alter it.
The source gloss weened for wēnde is modernized as thought; supposed; its Old English spelling and quantity are unchanged.
Cook dictionary division hyphens in gewrit and forlǣtan remain joined in the course word. Separate ge-writ and for-lǣtan divisions are explicit teaching support, not source respellings.
ge-scēop is a separate supplied prefix division. The reading itself remains exactly God gescēop heofonan and eorðan.
dohtor retains short o; scūfan retains Cook’s long ū; hȳdan retains the quantity printed in Cook Exercises V.18.9.
No Cook exercise prompt, assigned item, full paradigm or source passage is edited.
source_scope_limits: Visible front-vowel spelling is a useful default with lexical limits, not a complete historical derivation. y/ȳ are explicitly excluded as automatic c/g instructions.
The after-i/ī rule for noninitial c is not generalized to all front vowels. Back-vowel endings, consonant contact and named lexical exceptions remain distinct.
The single-g procedure first selects y versus non-y and only then applies the stopped/continuous distribution; a following consonant does not by itself force stopped g.
sc/cg/gg/ng combinations are handled before single-letter rules. Existing frosc/docga/sengan exceptions are supplied, not left for spelling inference.
The pronunciation practice makes no independent vocabulary, morphology or syntax-production claim.
